issues.title: Build bilingual static routes, templates and legacy aliases
issues.description:
Storyboard: /volume1/projects/leochai-website/tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md
Scenes / scope: §1 page map; all H/G/J/T/L/O/N routes; résumé and locale RSS
Build order: M1, step 1 (relative day 30 target).

Set up build-time Eleventy with content/en and content/zh outside generated site/, shared templates/assets, and a route manifest for seven core destinations. Emit real trailing-slash HTML, root English Home and /en/ alias, Simplified Chinese mirrors, stable cross-locale fragments and legacy alias documents. Build into temporary output, validate, then promote.

Key constraints

* No runtime locale router, language toggle, browser redirect, locale cookie or page-load translation.
* Root is English canonical/x-default; /en/ canonical points to /; correct lang/hreflang only for existing translations, revision-linked sources and explicit English-only article list.
* Support production / and preview /leochai-website/; preserve .nojekyll and CNAME [leochai.com](<http://leochai.com>); [publish.sh](<http://publish.sh>) only, no Actions/force-push.

Acceptance criteria (§14)

* §14 day 30 + checks 1–2: both core locales and legacy/deep links work without JS or NAS; assets, résumé, feeds, canonicals and fragments pass both deployment bases.
* Missing Chinese articles produce neither fake routes nor false alternate links.

## Feature-section work breakdown

* [LEO-112 · §1 · /en–/zh Eleventy build, canonical routes and legacy aliases](<https://linear.app/leochai/issue/LEO-112/1-en-zh-eleventy-build-canonical-routes-and-legacy-aliases>)
* [LEO-113 · §1 · Seven destinations, résumé, locale feeds and owner boundary](<https://linear.app/leochai/issue/LEO-113/1-seven-destinations-resume-locale-feeds-and-owner-boundary>)

## User-flow acceptance specs (§12)

* **F6 · Chinese visitor:** `/zh/` → mirrored core pages → locale event labels/shared budgets → Chinese Notes or explicitly English-only entry. No toggle/automatic switch.

Acceptance: exercise the applicable flow at this milestone, record the result and relevant failure behavior in the implementing child, and keep the authored/static baseline usable independently of later live activation. These sub-issues contain the full implementation requirements; this parent remains the feature rollup in its original milestone.

## Decision & build steps (2026-09-11)

**Decision (D1 — build & bilingual routing):**

* Eleventy 3.1.x, ESM config. Bundled `I18nPlugin` (defaultLanguage `en`, `errorMode: "allow-fallback"`) + `HtmlBasePlugin` + `@11ty/eleventy-plugin-rss` v2 (virtual-template Atom feeds per locale, language `en` / `zh-Hans`).
* Sources `content/en/` + `content/zh/` outside generated output. Pagination-over-array emits BOTH `/` (canonical English Home) and `/en/` (full alias, canonical → `/`). zh routes under `/zh/`; routing prefix and BCP-47 metadata kept separate (`lang="zh-Hans"`).
* Legacy alias families `/work/<slug>/` AND `/notes/.../` are real static HTML documents: meta refresh + visible link + canonical to destination + noindex. Work without JS. Fragments: a server-side alias cannot recover arbitrary old fragment semantics, so important legacy anchor IDs are preserved as real IDs in target pages' HTML; alias fixtures include fragment deep-links tested with JavaScript disabled.
* Central `content/_data/routes.js` manifest drives nav, hreflang, sitemap. Sitemap and hreflang list canonical routes only, never aliases. Translation completeness validated explicitly (allow-fallback does not enforce it); missing zh articles get no route and no false alternate link.
* Build per target with `--pathprefix` (`/` production, `/leochai-website/` preview). Each target is built, validated, and promoted separately — never rebuild between validate and promote.
* Absolute URLs (canonical/hreflang/RSS/sitemap) derive from `metadata.base = https://leochai.com/`, not pathPrefix. HtmlBasePlugin only rewrites HTML attributes: CSS `url()`, JSON fetch URLs, hand-written absolute URLs handled manually.
* Explicit ASCII slugs; explicit heading IDs shared across locales.
* Deploy: keep `scripts/publish.sh` (git-worktree, normal commit+push, no force-push). `gh-pages` npm package REJECTED (conflicts with no-force-push policy). `CNAME` + `.nojekyll` emitted into build output.

**Build steps (in order):**

1. LEO-112 — scaffold Eleventy ESM project, locale routing, dual `/`+`/en/` emit, aliases, canonical/hreflang.
2. LEO-113 — seven destinations, résumé, locale RSS feeds, owner boundary.
3. LEO-162 (under Release & acceptance) — harness validates this build on both prefix targets before promotion.

issues.title: Create shared visual, evidence, state and motion components
issues.description:
Storyboard: /volume1/projects/leochai-website/tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md
Scenes / scope: §1 globals; shared H/G/J/T/L/O/N components
Build order: M1, step 2 (relative day 30 target).

Implement the warm-paper typography, locale navigation/footer, inline proof blocks and distinct provenance/execution labels. Provide completed stills, transcripts and keyboard-accessible Play/Pause/Replay/Scrub controls for explanatory sequences. Define the evidence manifest so every run-backed exhibit can substantiate its claims.

Key constraints

* LIVE needs committed execution, run ID/server event time; RECORDED needs capture time/revision; UNKNOWN names missing evidence/failure. Fixtures/illustrations/local animation are source labels, never invented captures.
* Proof records repo, commit, capture date, input hash, provider/model, schema, redaction and contribution; distinguish measured from estimated metrics and upstream authorship.
* \~300 ms entrances; no loops/scroll-hijack; reduced motion shows numbered completed steps; focus visible, targets ≥44px, assets activate on demand.

Acceptance criteria (§14)

* §14 checks 1, 2, 8: visible conclusions survive no JS, failed assets and phone/reduced-motion/keyboard use.
* No replay/cache is LIVE; no unsupported metric or synthetic illustration mislabeled RECORDED.

## Feature-section work breakdown

* [LEO-114 · §1 · Global navigation, typography, state/proof and motion components](<https://linear.app/leochai/issue/LEO-114/1-global-navigation-typography-stateproof-and-motion-components>)
* [LEO-115 · §0 · Site-wide story, live-surface and authorship rules](<https://linear.app/leochai/issue/LEO-115/0-site-wide-story-live-surface-and-authorship-rules>)

## User-flow acceptance specs (§12)

* **F7 · Mobile/reduced motion:** diagrams readable; chat stacks; farm text timeline; optional rigs/viewers unloaded; numbered animation stills.
* **F8 · NAS/quota failure:** recorded farm and pipeline, authored Leo FAQ with unavailable answer state, functional Notes/contact/animations.

Acceptance: exercise the applicable flow at this milestone, record the result and relevant failure behavior in the implementing child, and keep the authored/static baseline usable independently of later live activation. These sub-issues contain the full implementation requirements; this parent remains the feature rollup in its original milestone.

## Decision & build steps (2026-09-11)

**Decision (D2 — motion & shared components):**

* Custom vanilla player (\~3 KB estimate — enforce a measured budget). State is a pure function of time `stateAt(model, t)`; rAF clock; Play/Pause/Replay buttons; native `input[type=range]` scrubber with `aria-valuetext`; step changes announced via `aria-live="polite"` (announce steps, not frames). Central registry enforces one active sequence.
* `prefers-reduced-motion` → completed final frame + numbered steps; "view as numbered steps" offered to everyone.
* Baseline HTML is the build-generated final frame — fully readable without JS. Bundled JSON is the only source of truth.
* anime.js v4 (MIT) is a fallback ONLY if hand-authoring keyframes proves too slow; deterministic state stays in our code, callbacks muted during seek. Rejected: Lottie/Rive/dotLottie, Scrollama, GSAP.
* Typography (D6) is owned by child LEO-161: Newsreader (display, Latin subset) + Source Sans 3 (UI, Latin subset) self-hosted WOFF2; Noto Serif SC 500 exact heading subsets for zh; system CJK body stack; ≤100 KB fonts/route measured.

**Build steps (in order):**

1. LEO-161 — typography pipeline (fonts + subsetting build) first; templates consume its tokens.
2. LEO-114 — global nav, typography tokens, state/proof components, the timeline-player component with full accessibility contract.
3. LEO-115 — site-wide story/live-surface/authorship rules applied across components.

issues.description:
Storyboard: /volume1/projects/leochai-website/tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md
Scenes / scope: G1–G2/G4; links to J1/T1/O1/L1 and O2–O5; F5

Create four ordered project rows: Jobs, farm, OpenCode and AI-Leo, each with static result image, problem, contribution and state. Link OpenCode feature tags directly to their stable scene fragments and finish with contact and a related personal Note. Reserve PC integration for its gated M3 issue.

Key constraints

* No filters, pagination, carousel, nested hub or hover-only information; Home retains direct case links.

Key constraints

* Configured guild/channel/owner allowlist; thread/message idempotency; no unrestricted coding-agent execution or public draft reads.

The shared world is persistent, not an episode. ## Agreed persistent-town direction — 2026-09-12

This feature owns the continuous life contract; detailed implementation belongs to the bounded children below. Latest user agreement supersedes the older short-episode specification and conflicting repository/storyboard text. This documentation pass authorizes no implementation, provisioning, paid calls, local edits or deployment.

One shared PERSISTENT town runs continuously on Leo's NAS. Everyone observes the same authoritative town, not a per-viewer sandbox or predetermined replay. Persistent objects, inventory, activities, character state, relationships and selected memories survive restarts. Continuity is desired even with no viewers; exact world-clock/offline catch-up semantics must be settled in LEO-144 before implementation.

### Approved five facets

* Mayor Leo: debate/leadership history.
* Engineer Leo: coding/building obsession; some high-school robotics.
* Teacher Leo: knowledgeable; teaches math; understanding and patient.
* Chef Leo: likes cooking; seeks new ingredients.
* Artsy Leo: listens to music, plays piano, likes anime; strong aesthetic taste.
  These are the supplied facts only; further characterization is for Leo to supply. Five AI versions/facets of Leo, not Leo speaking live. Fictional personas and world events are separate from approved real-life biography. Never invent degrees, dates, opinions or achievements.

### Life and conversation acceptance

* LLM-guided daily routines are context, not executable fixed scripts. Residents react to events/visitors, revise plans and develop relationships from actual interactions/outcomes without prescribed outcomes. HIGH personality/approved biography/usual schedule/long-term context; MEDIUM mood/emotion, energy/tiredness, plans, relationships/commitments; LOW surroundings/recent conversation/events/next action. Durable memory is separate from bounded model context (LEO-166/167).
* Deterministic engine ticks progress validated actions; LLM calls happen at decision boundaries/events. Model proposes intent; authoritative engine validates and commits rules, never direct text mutation (LEO-144/168).
* Visitors only TALK, text baseline. Persuasion may change permitted goals/actions; residents can refuse/reconsider. No direct object manipulation, rain/reset controls, steering API, arbitrary code/file/network authority.
* Exactly one visitor conversation per resident; others may approach another resident. Server-atomic capability/ownership and fenced lease across processes. Exactly FIVE REAL-WORLD minutes without an accepted visitor message ends the hold; assistant replies/heartbeats/rejected messages do not renew. Goodbye releases immediately; safely interrupt activity then resume/reassess. LEO-135 owns disconnect/reconnect/restart/late-response semantics; disconnect must not silently release immediately.
* One-resident-per-visitor, max-active-session fairness cap and absolute maximum duration are PROPOSALS, not approved rules. Microphone/audio is not required.

### Capacity, privacy and honesty gates

Before any town backend/inference provisioning, complete the NAS CPU/RAM/GPU and AI Society reuse audit and model-capacity decision in LEO-165. No paid calls or new capacity before that decision; an external model needs explicit Leo approval of budget, latency and privacy. Existing Jobs/AI-Leo and other allocations remain effective and cannot be transferred. This ticket records future work; no implementation is authorized by this documentation pass.
Continuous LLM life exceeds the old 40 attempts/day plan. Farm eight-attempt reservations, 16/day and two episodes/day are historical, not a new town allocation. Jobs/AI-Leo and unrelated budgets remain effective. World persistence is independent of model availability: queue/pause decisions honestly, allow only documented safe deterministic continuation, no fake dialogue/inference LIVE or catch-up call storms.
Conversation visibility is OPEN: private text/public resulting actions is suggested only. Leo must decide; LEO-131 owns disclosure, retention/deletion and provider visibility. No private files/kimaki history, raw private conversation logs or visitor rewriting of approved bio. Selected memories preserve provenance/untrusted status through summaries.

### Ordered ownership / dependencies

1. LEO-165 — read-only NAS/module audit and model-capacity decision, before backend/inference provisioning.
2. LEO-144 — shared authority, durable state, world-clock/offline policy and restart; LEO-131 — privacy decision. LEO-166 — five personas/layered context.
3. LEO-167 — durable provenance-aware memory/relationships; LEO-132/169 — bounded accounting/admission/security; LEO-135 — atomic talk/lease; LEO-136/142/143 — public snapshots/stream/truthful states.
4. LEO-168 — autonomous planning/execution using those contracts; LEO-170 under LEO-53 — live Canvas adapter.
5. LEO-171 — multi-client/lease/restart tests; LEO-172 — persuasion/injection/privacy/end-to-end evidence. LEO-164/53 retain pending visual review/Leo feedback.
6. LEO-76 — separate later Home integration, world-first composition followed by normal personal chapters; no whole-site game focus.

Children target roughly 0.5–2 engineer-day slices where feasible, not promised estimates; split after audit if needed. Parent is a rollup, not one giant implementation task.

### Visitor flows

F3: bilingual Tiny World/#live → immediate readable poster → same persistent town → talk to an available resident → observable allowed action/outcome. F6: mirrored EN/ZH core pages, locale labels/shared budgets, Chinese Notes or explicitly English-only entry; no automatic locale switch. F7: mobile/reduced-motion readable timeline, stacked text chat, optional rigs/viewers unloaded and numbered stills. F8: NAS/model unavailable → honest last-known/static world or separately labeled Illustration, completed pipeline baseline, authored Leo FAQ/unavailable answer state, functional Notes/contact/animations.

### Historical prototype / superseded episode work

LEO-53/90/91/163/164 and their existing comments/PRs document the authored 40s JSON illustration and art/Canvas review, not real autonomy. Art visual verdict remains pending. The former three-fictional-resident, six decisions ≥45s apart, six-minute ceiling, 60s zero-viewer shutdown, episode memory reset, no visitor dialogue and join/create-episode acceptance are superseded. Historical evidence/status is retained; do not implement those clauses for the persistent town. Captured real events may replay deterministically, but future LLM choices are not promised identical.

Who Leo is in three seconds

### Constraints and failure behavior (copied specification)

**Home alone closes the call.** Remove the unexplained old “3,799 jobs · 1 dependable record” placeholder. A defensible fixture claim is “7 synthetic observations → 3 canonical jobs; rerun adds 0,” explicitly labeled synthetic and tied to job-agent evidence. It is not production accuracy.

### Acceptance criteria

* What appears is implemented as specified above; the stated conclusion is visible and each action reaches its named destination.
* **Story:** a reader identifies Leo, three projects, email/résumé from Home without clicking. Every case has visible result, limit, authorship.
* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* **Motion:** phone viewport, keyboard, reduced motion, failed asset loads, transfer caps. Every animated feature communicates its result as a still.

Show the finished conclusion before interaction. Static HTML, conclusions and transcripts remain usable without JS or NAS. No model call on page load. Distinguish input provenance from LIVE / RECORDED / UNKNOWN execution; use server timestamps, capture revision and honest authorship. Keyboard, visible focus, ≥44px targets; reduced motion retains stills/numbered steps; optional assets load on activation.

Later normal-page chapters cover approved interests, projects and contact. Music, cooking and teaching may draw only on supplied facts; exact additional biography/wording is for Leo to approve. The older Waterloo + Wilfrid Laurier double-degree wording is not established by the supplied town facts and must not ship without separately verified Leo-approved biography. Ask Leo for exact biography/wording later; no invented facts. Keep a playful serious builder identity, not game-dev-only.

Do not implement during NOW prototype. Retain no inference triggered by Home load and no world run creation, static first paint/no-JS, reduced motion, keyboard access, honest evidence and <=500 KB initial compressed Home budget. Future passive observation attaches to the same persistent town already running independently of viewers (LEO-62/136/170), never starts/reserves an episode or pauses the server when Home is hidden. Any text chat entry routes to the resident conversation contract; no direct world controls. This unfinished ticket replaces the historical \~120px postcard assignment and is the future Home revision owner; LEO-50 remains Done history.

Separate later integration dependencies: LEO-164 review and Leo's world visual feedback, then LEO-170 validated live adapter or explicitly labeled Illustration/static baseline. Keep more-than-half-screen world + name/hello followed by normal personal chapters; whole site is not game-focused. No Home implementation in this documentation task.

issues.description:
## Current authority — 2026-09-12

Latest agreed persistent-town direction (2026-09-12) is owned by LEO-62 and its bounded children; it supersedes conflicting short-episode requirements and older repository text. This issue retains the art/illustration prototype scope below and does not claim implemented autonomy. Existing authored 40s JSON trace is Illustration, not a captured run or LIVE. Backend/inference provisioning waits for LEO-165; no implementation or spend in this documentation pass. Wave 1 Home remains rejected/CP2 unapproved; Leo's world visual verdict is pending and Home integration is separately later in LEO-76. Retain blue off-white, purple ink, pastels/turquoise and subtle Miku hints; sharp edges, hard shadows, forced grid breaks, gradient/word bans and two-pass cap are not requirements.

Own concise bilingual introduction adjacent to the world. Describe five AI versions/facets of Leo sharing one persistent town through everyday activities: Mayor (debate/leadership), Engineer (coding/building; some high-school robotics), Teacher (knowledgeable, math, understanding/patient), Chef (cooking/new ingredients), Artsy (music/piano/anime/aesthetic taste). These are supplied facts only; fictional personas/events are separate from approved biography, not Leo speaking live. Clearly label Bundled fixture / original or licensed illustration as applicable, and explain current deterministic prototype with no backend/inference. issues.title: L1 · Authored biography, projects and skills
issues.description:
### What appears

Authored biography, dated projects, skills Leo says he is most comfortable with, portrait

### Visitor understands

Actual information without talking to a bot

### Actions → destinations

Résumé / email / project links

Routes (en or zh; stable fragments): Home `/en/` or `/zh/` (English root `/`); G `/<lang>/projects/`; J `/<lang>/work/job-matching/#preview`; T `/<lang>/work/tiny-world/#live`; L `/<lang>/leo/#ask`; O `/<lang>/work/opencode/` (`#debate`, `#autocompact`, `#agent-pool`, `#xray`); N `/<lang>/notes/` and `/<lang>/notes/<slug>/`; résumé `/assets/leo-chai-resume.pdf`; email uses mailto.

### Constraints and failure behavior (copied specification)

### AI-Leo retrieval architecture

* Start with approved bio, résumé, public project summaries, short opinion answers. Leo's home audio/video adds evidence when recorded; it is not a launch dependency. Never ingest general kimaki history, DMs, calendars, NAS folders, or Jellyfin libraries.
* Private ingestion stores selected originals on the NAS. RQ CPU transcription processes recordings; Leo corrects/approves transcript and publishable excerpts. Only approved excerpts enter the public corpus. Raw home recordings remain private; media citations require separately approved clips.
* Postgres stores source ID, approval, date, language, revision, public anchor, optional timecode, supersession links. Chunk \~300 tokens with 50-token overlap. Version a small lexical index; Chinese uses explicit segmentation/character n-grams. Maintain approved bilingual aliases for skills/project names.
* Reuse AI Society's evidence/validity concepts and compatible contracts through a pinned adapter. Its production embedding adapter is unfinished: do not instantiate it or change research thresholds to ship the website. **First release is lexical retrieval plus generation; RAG does not require a vector database.** Defer semantic embeddings until they improve a held-out question set.
* `POST /api/demos/leo/answers`: ≤500 characters, at most two previous turns, signed 15-minute session. Retrieve up to four approved passages, ≤1,200 tokens; total prompt ≤2,500 tokens. No matching evidence → immediate abstention, zero model calls. “Current” facts use latest approved nonsuperseded source and show its date; conflicts/staleness do not become current fact.
* RQ makes one free request, ≤400 output tokens, no model retry, 35-second total deadline. Schema: answer, cited source IDs, unsupported flag. Reject unknown citations. Distinguish Leo's stated opinion from synthesis; never invent a stronger skill ranking. Citation validation cannot guarantee entailment; evaluate separately.
* Return validated answer plus excerpts. Cache only three public starter questions by locale/corpus revision/prompt/model; outputs say RECORDED. Arbitrary questions stay ephemeral, expire after 15 minutes, never update Leo's memory or enter permanent conversation logs.
* Before submission: “Your question and public source excerpts are sent to an external model provider. Don't include private information.” Keep routing privacy restrictions fixed; incompatible provider → source-only fallback, not relaxed settings. Outage shows authored FAQ and `UNKNOWN — no answer generated`.

### Anime character decision

Keep anime identity. Ship an original/commissioned **still first**, credited with rights. Day 90 permits a Live2D rig only in L3 if optional download ≤2 MB and asset/runtime rights are checked. States: idle-still, brief question-sent motion, one answer-ready gesture. No constant loop, fake lip-sync, camera tracking, microphone, voice cloning, or floating mascot. It reflects application events, not emotions of a digital person. Rig/load/WebGL failure leaves still and text Q&A intact. Zero model calls for animation.

### Acceptance criteria

Milestone interpretation: this child owns the day-30 authored/static/replay scene. Apply the checks below to the bundled evidence and presentation; live execution, runtime fault injection and the AI-Leo generated-answer evaluation are implemented and verified by the separate day-60/day-90 live parents (LEO-62, LEO-63, LEO-67). Those later implementations do not block acceptance of a truthful static scene.

* What appears is implemented as specified above; the stated conclusion is visible and each action reaches its named destination.
* **Story:** a reader identifies Leo, three projects, email/résumé from Home without clicking. Every case has visible result, limit, authorship.
* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* **Motion:** phone viewport, keyboard, reduced motion, failed asset loads, transfer caps. Every animated feature communicates its result as a still.
* **AI-Leo:** freeze 24 questions: eight factual, four opinions, four current/correction, four unsupported/private, four injection attempts, distributed across English/Chinese. Require approved valid citations for factual claims, no invented biography/opinion, correct supersession, abstention on every unsupported case. Leo reviews voice/meaning. Any violation blocks free-form Q&A; authored FAQ ships. This is a release check, not a claimed accuracy benchmark.

Show the finished conclusion before interaction. Static HTML, conclusions and transcripts remain usable without JS or NAS. No model call on page load. Distinguish input provenance from LIVE / RECORDED / UNKNOWN execution; use server timestamps, capture revision and honest authorship. Keyboard, visible focus, ≥44px targets; reduced motion retains stills/numbered steps; optional assets load on activation.

Specification: revised 2026-09-10, `tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md`; requirements are reproduced here so this issue can be implemented from Linear.

issues.title: §1 · /en–/zh Eleventy build, canonical routes and legacy aliases
issues.description:
### Concrete `/en`–`/zh` static-build strategy

* Keep sources outside generated `site/`: `content/en/`, `content/zh/`, route manifest, shared templates, asset manifests. Use **Eleventy as a build-time generator**, run locally or by the NAS publisher. No runtime locale router.
* Emit actual `index.html` files for every route, including `site/en/work/tiny-world/index.html` and its Chinese counterpart. Root `site/index.html` renders the same English Home source. English internal navigation uses `/en/...`; Chinese uses `/zh/...`. **No UI language toggle, browser-language redirect, or locale cookie.**
* `/` is canonical for English Home; `/en/` is a complete alias with canonical `/`. Other English pages are canonical under `/en/`. Set `lang`, translated metadata, and `hreflang="en"` / `hreflang="zh-Hans"` for existing pairs; root is `x-default`. Use Simplified Chinese. Slugs and fragments match across locales.
* Mirror every core page at launch. Translations record their source revision. Publish translated articles when ready; do not silently insert English into a Chinese article. Chinese Notes has an explicitly labeled “English articles awaiting translation” list. Missing Chinese articles get no generated route or false alternate-language link.
* Generate legacy `/work/<slug>/` and `/notes/.../` alias documents with visible links, canonical metadata, and a small redirect preserving fragments. These still work without JavaScript. No Pages rewrite or SPA 404 dependence.
* Build links/assets using a deployment base; verify production `/` and preview `/leochai-website/`. Share images, traces, and animation assets across locales; translate captions/transcripts. Backend events use localized event codes; original utterances retain a language label. No model translation on page load.
* Build to temporary output, validate, then promote to `site/`. Preserve `.nojekyll` and required `CNAME` value `leochai.com`. Publish through `./scripts/publish.sh`; **no GitHub Actions or force-push**.
* **Host decision:** preserve apex `leochai.com` per `AGENTS.md`. `www.leochai.com/` is an English-root entry point through the standard redirect to `leochai.com/`; it does not require `/en/`. This interprets Leo's request as English content at root, not retaining `www` in the address bar. Pages pairs apex and `www` according to its canonical host. [GitHub custom-domain documentation](<https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site>).
* Release discrepancy: README proposes a `www` cutover, AGENTS mandates apex, and the inspected working tree lacks `site/CNAME`. Prepare the release using the apex rule and restore that file before publishing. **Do not touch the old** `TheLeoChai.github.io` **repo without Leo's approval.** Verify the full artifact first; domain cutover is a separate deployment step.

### Page map changes

The original five core destinations were Home, three work pages, and Notes, plus article instances. The revision has **seven core destinations**: add Projects and Meet Leo. PC assembly lives within Projects, not on an eighth page. Articles use one shared template. Owner tools are outside the public site.

`<lang>` means `en` or `zh`. Use trailing slashes; keep fragment identifiers stable across languages.

| Destination | New URL | Change / purpose |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Home | `/en/`, `/zh/`; `/` serves English Home | Immediate pitch, specimen, three primary cards, personal introduction |
| Projects | `/<lang>/projects/` | New finite gallery: Jobs, Tiny World, OpenCode, AI-Leo, then PC when ready |
| Job Matching | `/<lang>/work/job-matching/` | Case study plus bounded website chat preview at `#preview` |
| Tiny World | `/<lang>/work/tiny-world/` | Farm adaptation plus shared episode at `#live` |
| OpenCode | `/<lang>/work/opencode/` | Four animated feature stories with direct fragment links |
| Meet Leo | `/<lang>/leo/` | Biography, opinions, memory-backed Q&A at `#ask`; avatar belongs here |
| Notes | `/<lang>/notes/`, `/<lang>/notes/<slug>/` | AI/technology, build reflections, and recipes together |
| PC assembly | `/<lang>/projects/#pc-assembly` | Inline exhibit, no empty “coming soon” destination |
| Résumé / feeds | `/assets/leo-chai-resume.pdf`, `/<lang>/rss.xml` | One factual résumé source; feeds contain published locale articles |
| Owner launchpad | Private NAS `/owner/`, over Tailscale only | Separate origin outside `site/`; existing Jellyfin and owner tools |

### Acceptance criteria

* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* Emit and validate every specified core route in both locales, root canonical/alias metadata, revision-linked translations and both deployment bases.

Specification: revised 2026-09-10, `tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md`; requirements are reproduced here so this issue can be implemented from Linear.

issues.description:
## 0. Laws and explicit revisions

1. **No puzzle required.** Show the conclusion, finished state, and concrete example before interaction. Motion explains an already visible result.
2. **One shared live simulation: Tiny World.** Explicitly revise “one live demo total” to admit two bounded, opt-in tools: a Job Matching run and an AI-Leo answer. These are additional live features; calling them previews does not erase their cost. No model calls on page load. No public OpenCode terminal. The farm runs short episodes, not 24/7 inference.
3. **Everything past Home is opt-in depth.** Add one Projects gallery. Home still links directly to the strongest case studies; the gallery is never a mandatory intermediate stop.
4. **Proof is inline.** No evidence drawers, nested demo hub, canvas dedup graph, standalone build-log, or standalone infrastructure visualization. Technical disclosures contain supporting detail, not conclusions.
5. **Uncertainty stays visible.** Keep the ambiguous merge, rejected world action, unsupported personal answer, and failed coding-tool run.
6. **Truthful states:** `LIVE`, `RECORDED`, `UNKNOWN`. A live connection does not prove live inference. Label input provenance and output execution separately. Never say “waking server…” without a real wake mechanism.
7. **Static first.** Public routes, articles, conclusions, images, and replays come from GitHub Pages. FastAPI on the NAS owns live work. NAS failure must not prevent reading the site.
8. **Honest authorship.** Distinguish Leo's projects, upstream modifications, companion tools, third-party components, licensed/generated art, illustrations, and verified captures. AI-Leo is not Leo speaking live.
9. **Personality has a budget.** Keep anime and recipes. Give the farm warmth. Reserve PC assembly for one small gallery exhibit. No game-lobby Home or floating avatar everywhere.

| Feature / scenes | Runs live | Recorded / bundled baseline | Free-model use | Failure result |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Locale mirrors / all | Nothing | Full locale HTML; shared assets | 0 at request time | Missing article translation explicitly listed as English-only |
| Farm / H4, G1, T2–T5 | One shared short episode; ticks + bounded decisions | Verified trace/still; separately labeled synthetic variants | ≤8 attempts/episode, ≤2 episodes/day | Failed episode marked; last frame; separate replay |
| Jobs / J2–J5 | Real pipeline on fixtures, website outbox/review | Completed trace and identity fixtures | ≤3 attempts/run, ≤4 fresh runs/day | Incomplete stage, no invented score; separate replay |

| Anime / L3 | Local event gesture if gate passes | Still avatar | 0 | Still; text unaffected |

issues.description:
Launch content: “A duplicate is an identity problem,” “Provenance beats accuracy,” a rejected-design/failure post, and a real recipe from Leo. Publish supplied material; do not invent his opinions or a recipe to fill slots.

### Concrete `/en`–`/zh` static-build strategy

* Keep sources outside generated `site/`: `content/en/`, `content/zh/`, route manifest, shared templates, asset manifests. Use **Eleventy as a build-time generator**, run locally or by the NAS publisher. No runtime locale router.
* Emit actual `index.html` files for every route, including `site/en/work/tiny-world/index.html` and its Chinese counterpart. Root `site/index.html` renders the same English Home source. English internal navigation uses `/en/...`; Chinese uses `/zh/...`. **No UI language toggle, browser-language redirect, or locale cookie.**
* `/` is canonical for English Home; `/en/` is a complete alias with canonical `/`. Other English pages are canonical under `/en/`. Set `lang`, translated metadata, and `hreflang="en"` / `hreflang="zh-Hans"` for existing pairs; root is `x-default`. Use Simplified Chinese. Slugs and fragments match across locales.
* Mirror every core page at launch. Translations record their source revision. Publish translated articles when ready; do not silently insert English into a Chinese article. Chinese Notes has an explicitly labeled “English articles awaiting translation” list. Missing Chinese articles get no generated route or false alternate-language link.
* Generate legacy `/work/<slug>/` and `/notes/.../` alias documents with visible links, canonical metadata, and a small redirect preserving fragments. These still work without JavaScript. No Pages rewrite or SPA 404 dependence.
* Build links/assets using a deployment base; verify production `/` and preview `/leochai-website/`. Share images, traces, and animation assets across locales; translate captions/transcripts. Backend events use localized event codes; original utterances retain a language label. No model translation on page load.
* Build to temporary output, validate, then promote to `site/`. Preserve `.nojekyll` and required `CNAME` value `leochai.com`. Publish through `./scripts/publish.sh`; **no GitHub Actions or force-push**.
* **Host decision:** preserve apex `leochai.com` per `AGENTS.md`. `www.leochai.com/` is an English-root entry point through the standard redirect to `leochai.com/`; it does not require `/en/`. This interprets Leo's request as English content at root, not retaining `www` in the address bar. Pages pairs apex and `www` according to its canonical host. [GitHub custom-domain documentation](<https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site>).
* Release discrepancy: README proposes a `www` cutover, AGENTS mandates apex, and the inspected working tree lacks `site/CNAME`. Prepare the release using the apex rule and restore that file before publishing. **Do not touch the old** `TheLeoChai.github.io` **repo without Leo's approval.** Verify the full artifact first; domain cutover is a separate deployment step.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Story:** a reader identifies Leo, three projects, email/résumé from Home without clicking. Every case has visible result, limit, authorship.
* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* **Publisher/privacy:** wrong author/stale Publish rejected; duplicate events yield one draft; malformed media/Markdown cannot execute scripts; deployment recoverable; no originals/drafts/secrets/Jellyfin/private text in public output/history. Published content hash verified.
* Only supplied/approved material ships; no invented opinions or recipe; feeds include only published locale articles.

### Backend action / failure

Private Postgres draft; RQ generates Markdown/front matter. First line defaults title; collision-safe stable slug; photo order retained. Zero LLM required. Optional cleanup is one bounded free call; cannot invent quantities, times, opinions, captions, facts. Show edits and original.

Extend **existing kimaki**, using a private channel such as `#site-drafts`. Reuse personal-api's Postgres/Redis/RQ infrastructure, but add **private** draft tables/routes, not publicly readable `/api/posts` or album reads. Published Markdown/media in Git are the public source of truth; API holds workflow receipts/drafts. Notes require no NAS reads after publication. Back up drafts, originals, receipts.

Publisher credentials are repo-scoped, separate from inference keys, unavailable to public workers/models. Fixed build commands operate on content only; uploads cannot alter templates, scripts, dependencies, or destinations. Document setup/recovery in `services/site-publisher/README.md` before unattended publishing. One preview/one click replaces manual Git work without publishing casual chatter automatically.

### Launch budget: $0 in purchased inference

OpenRouter currently documents **50 requests/day and 20/minute** for unfunded free-model use; qualifying credit purchases increase the daily allowance. More keys do not create account quota. Availability is opportunistic, not an SLA. [OpenRouter limits](<https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits>), [published free-tier figures](<https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/how-to-get-the-lowest-cost-llm-inference-on-openrouter/>).

**Site ceiling: 40 upstream attempts per UTC day, six/minute, one in flight globally.** Deployment checks actual limits, eligibility, competing account usage; reduce this ceiling when needed. No paid fallback, auto-top-up, quota-evading key rotation, or trial-credit dependence. Free describes inference billing; NAS electricity/storage/bandwidth/maintenance still cost something.

| Reservation | Attempts/day | Max input/output tokens per attempt | Buys |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Farm | 16 | 2,000 / 256 | Two episodes, each six decisions plus two retries |
| Jobs | 12 | 3,000 / 500 | Four runs, each two scores plus one retry |
| AI-Leo | 8 | 2,500 / 400 | Eight uncached answers, no retry |
| Optional post polish | 2 | 4,000 / 1,000 | Two cleanups; long posts use deterministic formatting |
| Verification reserve | 2 | 3,000 / 500 | Smoke probes, not continual inference health checks |
| **Total** | **40** | **≤102,000 input / ≤16,296 output tokens/day** | Hard ceilings, not promised throughput |

* A server-side gateway holds the OpenRouter key. Pin tested `:free` model IDs/provider policy per feature in deployment config. No browser model/provider/key selection; no random free router for recorded comparisons. Verify zero-priced routes and schema/language behavior before release. Record exact model ID in captures; retired/unavailable model → fail closed. Model selection is a deployment gate, not a promise that today's model exists in 90 days.
* Redis atomically reserves each run's maximum attempts and enforces shared caps. Postgres durably records reservations/attempts so Redis restart cannot replenish quota. Reserve before enqueue; idempotency prevents double reservation. Failed calls/retries count conservatively. Release safely expired unused reservations; never refund unknown sent attempts. Disable implicit SDK retries and model-fallback loops.
* Budgets span locales/features and the provider account. No automatic transfer between allocations. Other account usage reduces availability; provider 429 overrides the local ledger.

## 12. User flows

* **F1 · 90-second lead:** H1 identity → H2 resolved specimen → H3 accomplishments → H4 farm image → H5 person → H6 contact. Zero required clicks or inference.
* **F2 · Engineer:** uncertain pair → J2 → completed J4 transcript → optional sample → J5 evidence → OpenCode animation → email.
* **F3 · Farm sharer:** `/<lang>/work/tiny-world/#live` → captured farm immediately → join/reserve episode → resident observation → adaptation label.
* **F4 · Meet Leo:** H5 → authored L1/L2 → L3 question → citations → email when unsupported.
* **F5 · Casual explorer:** gallery → PC clip → recipe → RSS. Engineering knowledge optional.
* **F6 · Chinese visitor:** `/zh/` → mirrored core pages → locale event labels/shared budgets → Chinese Notes or explicitly English-only entry. No toggle/automatic switch.
* **F7 · Mobile/reduced motion:** diagrams readable; chat stacks; farm text timeline; optional rigs/viewers unloaded; numbered animation stills.
* **F8 · NAS/quota failure:** recorded farm and pipeline, authored Leo FAQ with unavailable answer state, functional Notes/contact/animations.
* **F9 · Publish dinner:** private Discord photos/text → draft → private preview → one Publish click → verified article link. No terminal/Markdown editing.
* **F10 · Owner evening:** Tailscale → private launchpad → existing Jellyfin sign-in. No public-site payload.

### Global elements

| Element | Spec |
| -- | -- |
| Nav | `Leo Chai — Projects · Notes · Résumé`. Name links to locale Home; current section underlined. No dropdowns. Meet Leo is linked from Home and Projects. |
| Footer | Email · GitHub · locale RSS · “Static pages; live experiments run on my server at home.” Infrastructure explanation is inline, not another page. |
| Typography | Warm paper, dark ink, vermillion accent; serif statements, sans UI, mono actual data. Chinese typography retains hierarchy and readable line lengths. |
| Motion | One \~300ms entrance per element. Explanatory sequences run on Play, with Pause/Replay/Scrub, never automatic loops. Reduced motion shows completed diagrams and numbered steps. No scroll-hijack. |
| State chips | LIVE includes run ID and last event time; RECORDED includes capture time and revision; UNKNOWN names missing evidence/failure. Server timestamps, not connection status alone. |
| Bundled content | `Bundled fixture`, `Illustration`, `Local 3D animation` are source labels, not a fourth execution chip. A synthetic illustration is not a recorded run. |
| Page weight | Home initial compressed transfer ≤500 KB excluding optional résumé. No WebGL, Live2D runtime, or video download on Home. Optional detail assets load on activation. |
| Access | Conclusions/transcripts work without JS; keyboard controls, visible focus, touch targets ≥44px. Do not announce every farm tick through a screen reader. |
| Proof manifest | Run-backed exhibits record repo, commit, capture date, input/scenario hash, provider/model, trace schema, redaction note, and Leo's contribution. Metrics link to evidence. |

### Acceptance criteria

* **Story:** a reader identifies Leo, three projects, email/résumé from Home without clicking. Every case has visible result, limit, authorship.
* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* **Publisher/privacy:** wrong author/stale Publish rejected; duplicate events yield one draft; malformed media/Markdown cannot execute scripts; deployment recoverable; no originals/drafts/secrets/Jellyfin/private text in public output/history. Published content hash verified.
* **Motion:** phone viewport, keyboard, reduced motion, failed asset loads, transfer caps. Every animated feature communicates its result as a still.
* Both core locales and preview base pass; a draft publishes and failed build preserves the old site; live inference, PC and rig do not block.

issues.title: §1 · Apex-domain release artifact and discrepancy runbook
issues.description:
### Concrete `/en`–`/zh` static-build strategy

* Keep sources outside generated `site/`: `content/en/`, `content/zh/`, route manifest, shared templates, asset manifests. Use **Eleventy as a build-time generator**, run locally or by the NAS publisher. No runtime locale router.
* Emit actual `index.html` files for every route, including `site/en/work/tiny-world/index.html` and its Chinese counterpart. Root `site/index.html` renders the same English Home source. English internal navigation uses `/en/...`; Chinese uses `/zh/...`. **No UI language toggle, browser-language redirect, or locale cookie.**
* `/` is canonical for English Home; `/en/` is a complete alias with canonical `/`. Other English pages are canonical under `/en/`. Set `lang`, translated metadata, and `hreflang="en"` / `hreflang="zh-Hans"` for existing pairs; root is `x-default`. Use Simplified Chinese. Slugs and fragments match across locales.
* Mirror every core page at launch. Translations record their source revision. Publish translated articles when ready; do not silently insert English into a Chinese article. Chinese Notes has an explicitly labeled “English articles awaiting translation” list. Missing Chinese articles get no generated route or false alternate-language link.
* Generate legacy `/work/<slug>/` and `/notes/.../` alias documents with visible links, canonical metadata, and a small redirect preserving fragments. These still work without JavaScript. No Pages rewrite or SPA 404 dependence.
* Build links/assets using a deployment base; verify production `/` and preview `/leochai-website/`. Share images, traces, and animation assets across locales; translate captions/transcripts. Backend events use localized event codes; original utterances retain a language label. No model translation on page load.
* Build to temporary output, validate, then promote to `site/`. Preserve `.nojekyll` and required `CNAME` value `leochai.com`. Publish through `./scripts/publish.sh`; **no GitHub Actions or force-push**.
* **Host decision:** preserve apex `leochai.com` per `AGENTS.md`. `www.leochai.com/` is an English-root entry point through the standard redirect to `leochai.com/`; it does not require `/en/`. This interprets Leo's request as English content at root, not retaining `www` in the address bar. Pages pairs apex and `www` according to its canonical host. [GitHub custom-domain documentation](<https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site>).
* Release discrepancy: README proposes a `www` cutover, AGENTS mandates apex, and the inspected working tree lacks `site/CNAME`. Prepare the release using the apex rule and restore that file before publishing. **Do not touch the old** `TheLeoChai.github.io` **repo without Leo's approval.** Verify the full artifact first; domain cutover is a separate deployment step.

Farm/public traces contain fictional data only; Leo citations contain approved excerpts only. Logs keep IDs/timings/error codes/counters, not raw questions/secrets. Rate-limit hashes expire after 24h; redacted NAS demo captures after seven days. Promote reviewed captures into the static bundle deliberately.

Before implementation, record per-service hosting in `services/README.md`; overall NAS choice is already recorded. Update `docs/infra.md` when actual infra changes. Its recovered-source/container notes conflict with older “not in repo” / “root-only” sections; resolve through deployment inspection, not assumptions.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* Prepare and verify the full artifact with CNAME [leochai.com](<http://leochai.com>); inspect conflicting documentation; old-repo cutover requires Leo's separate approval.

issues.title: §11 · NAS architecture, service inventory and worker isolation
issues.description:
## Town integration gate — 2026-09-12

LEO-165 owns actual NAS CPU/RAM/GPU and AI Society reuse/model-capacity audit before town backend/inference provisioning. Its supplied source evidence is not a deployment test. Keep existing NAS FastAPI/Postgres/Redis/RQ/Caddy/DDNS and static GitHub Pages; no migration/new capacity. LEO-144 owns durable shared world; in-memory AI Society world/memory is not already persistent. LEO-169 owns bounded public admission. Unrelated platform scopes below remain effective.

Use the existing decision: **kawaiinas + Caddy + DDNS**, `https://api.leochai.com`, FastAPI/Postgres/Redis/RQ. No cloud GPU, new host, or paid always-on inference. Give each integration a self-contained `services/` folder, README, and public scene link. No backend code in `site/`.

| Component | Responsibility / boundary |
| -- | -- |
| Pages | Locale HTML, conclusions, traces, animations, posters, published media. No keys/private drafts. |
| Caddy + demo FastAPI | HTTPS, limits, signed capabilities, snapshot/SSE, validation/admission; exact-origin CORS. No arbitrary URL proxy. |
| Redis | Limits, ephemeral sessions, queues, run lock, bounded event streams; not sole accounting ledger or world authority. |
| Postgres | Runs, authoritative world/events/memories, approved Leo corpus, attempt ledger, separately protected publishing tables; transactional event outbox. |
| RQ | Separate `world`, `jobs`, `leo`, `publish` queues/workers. Public workers lack Git/Discord credentials, Docker socket, owner storage, personal candidate files. |
| Inference gateway | Serial admission, free-model allowlist, privacy policy, receipts, deadlines/output caps; no NAS-access tools. |
| Job storage | Per-run SQLite, deleted after an hour; no access to real job database. |
| Owner/publisher | Tailscale-only preview/launchpad, authenticated internal bot route, isolated checkout, narrow deploy authority. Public requests cannot enqueue publishing. |

Public town world events are fictional and approved biography stays separately sourced; visitor conversation visibility is OPEN under LEO-131 and cannot be treated as automatically public fictional data. Leo citations contain approved excerpts only. Logs keep IDs/timings/error codes/counters, not raw questions/secrets. Rate-limit hashes expire after 24h; redacted NAS demo captures after seven days; this capture TTL does not delete the persistent town or decide selected visitor-memory retention. Promote reviewed captures into the static bundle deliberately.

Before implementation, record per-service hosting in `services/README.md`; overall NAS choice is already recorded. Update `docs/infra.md` when actual infra changes. Its recovered-source/container notes conflict with older “not in repo” / “root-only” sections; resolve through deployment inspection, not assumptions.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Accounting:** concurrent creation/retries/worker interruption/Redis restart/model retirement/429/malformed JSON cannot bypass budgets, make paid calls, or cross sessions. Probes count.
* **Publisher/privacy:** wrong author/stale Publish rejected; duplicate events yield one draft; malformed media/Markdown cannot execute scripts; deployment recoverable; no originals/drafts/secrets/Jellyfin/private text in public output/history. Published content hash verified.
* Record per-service hosting before implementation; self-contained service folders and READMEs include local operation, host and public scene URL; no backend runtime in site/.

Reuse this privacy/retention owner; roughly 0.5–2 engineer-days for a decided-policy projection/redaction slice, not a full integration estimate. LEO-165 capacity/model gate precedes backend/inference provisioning. Jobs/AI-Leo/publishing privacy and retention below are unchanged; their ephemeral sessions do not govern persistent-town memories.

* Specify selected-memory retention duration/selection limits, deletion/redaction request process and identity proof, treatment of derived summaries, event projections/captures and backup deletion/expiry. * Define approved character fact correction/versioning separately from visitor memory deletion. LEO-166 owns approved facts; LEO-167 implements memory/relationship storage and redaction propagation; LEO-136/170 enforce public/private projections.
* Test two visitors/residents cannot access forbidden sources, redaction reaches derived retrieval/projections, backup restore cannot silently revive deleted data, and no private text leaks in logs/errors/captures.

Dependencies: policy decision before LEO-167/169/135/136 public activation; LEO-165 for model/provider disclosure. This issue records work and open decisions, not user approval of a suggested default.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Accounting:** concurrent creation/retries/worker interruption/Redis restart/model retirement/429/malformed JSON cannot bypass budgets, make paid calls, or cross sessions. Probes count.

issues.title: API · Resident text conversation, atomic ownership and five-minute idle lease
issues.description:
## Current route ownership — persistent town

Replace the old public POST /api/demos/world/runs create/join-episode contract with resident conversation claim/message/goodbye operations on the existing shared town. Exact route names/request schemas are an implementation contract to document here; no world creation/reset endpoint. This reuses the existing API child rather than adding a duplicate. Planning target 1–2 engineer-days for server lease/API slice; split transport/UI separately (LEO-170). Before any town backend/inference provisioning, complete the NAS CPU/RAM/GPU and AI Society reuse audit and model-capacity decision in LEO-165. No paid calls or new capacity before that decision; an external model needs explicit Leo approval of budget, latency and privacy. Existing Jobs/AI-Leo and other allocations remain effective and cannot be transferred. This ticket records future work; no implementation is authorized by this documentation pass.

## Agreed behavior

* Visitors TALK only, text baseline; no microphone/audio requirement. No object manipulation, rain/reset, steering API or arbitrary code/file/network access. Persuasion can affect allowed resident plans; refusal/reconsideration is valid.
* Each resident supports one visitor conversation at a time across every server process. Other visitors cannot talk to that resident while held and may approach another. Use server-atomic ownership with an unforgeable resident-scoped capability and lease/fencing version, not an in-memory per-worker flag.
* Accepted visitor speech/message sets last_accepted_visitor_message_at using server real time. At exactly 300 real-world seconds with no accepted visitor message, the hold is invalid and ends. Model responses, heartbeats, watching, transport reconnect, rejected payloads and duplicate message retries do not extend it. Never tie idle to simulation ticks.
* Explicit goodbye releases immediately and idempotently. Safely interrupt/pause current activity on claim; after release/expiry resume or reassess with engine validation. No promise the resident must obey persuasion.
* Validate ownership/version/expiry atomically when accepting a message and again before applying any queued/model result. Fence late replies from changing world, plan, memories or published dialogue after lease/version change. Define idempotency keys for claims/messages/releases and consistent busy/expired/invalid responses.
* Persist/recover reservation, owner, last accepted message time and fencing version; API/worker/Redis restart cannot duplicate ownership or extend idle. Expired reservations are reconciled from durable server timestamps before any accepted write, even if a sweeper/job is delayed.
* Disconnect is NOT silently immediate release. Decide authenticated reconnect behavior explicitly before implementation: capability reattachment/rotation, lost-capability handling and server-restart fence recovery, always bounded by the five-minute visitor-idle deadline. Reconnect itself cannot renew.
* Decide initial claim semantics (atomic claim with first accepted message, or explicit pre-message hold policy) so an empty claim cannot invent unlimited idle. This is OPEN implementation design, not a change to the agreed five-minute rule.
* One-resident-per-visitor, max-active-session fairness cap and absolute maximum duration are PROPOSALS awaiting Leo, not acceptance requirements. Conversation visibility is OPEN in LEO-131; private text/public resulting actions is only suggested.

## Security / integration acceptance

Exact-origin checks plus capabilities, bounded payloads/rates/finite queues; no raw private conversation logging or privileged worker credentials. LEO-169 handles inference admission after model/privacy gates. Public snapshots expose only approved state; capability-authenticated private responses must not leak to other visitors. Postgres authority/Redis coordination/RQ on existing NAS; static Pages frontend remains unchanged in architecture.

## Tests / dependencies

Depends on LEO-165, LEO-144 state/fencing, LEO-131 privacy and LEO-169 admission before public inference. Coordinate LEO-168 pause/resume.
Tests: simultaneous cross-process claims yield one winner; another resident can be approached; only accepted message renews; 299.999s vs 300s boundary; goodbye immediate; expiry resumes/reassesses activity; stale reply after expiry/reclaim cannot mutate; reconnect/restart/delayed jobs preserve exact idle and reservations; cross-resident capabilities/replayed messages fail. LEO-171 owns full scenario evidence.

## Historical supersession

Former fixed-scenario shared-episode reservation, no dialogue, three actors, six decisions/six minutes, zero-viewer stop and episode memory reset are obsolete town acceptance, preserved only in issue history. No implementation/status change is implied.

issues.description:
## Scope and gate — 2026-09-12

Reuse this existing engine child for a bounded authoritative state/persistence slice, planning target 1–2 engineer-days after clock policy is resolved; split if needed. Single shared persistent NAS town, five Leo facets, no per-viewer worlds or predetermined replay. Before any town backend/inference provisioning, complete the NAS CPU/RAM/GPU and AI Society reuse audit and model-capacity decision in LEO-165. No paid calls or new capacity before that decision; an external model needs explicit Leo approval of budget, latency and privacy. Existing Jobs/AI-Leo and other allocations remain effective and cannot be transferred. This ticket records future work; no implementation is authorized by this documentation pass.

## Decide before implementation

Document world time scale/timezone, deterministic tick/progress unit, how due actions are ordered and how wall-clock gaps/restarts are handled. Continuous simulation is desired; exact offline catch-up policy is OPEN. Explicitly decide whether/how safe ongoing actions advance during downtime, limits on catch-up, skipped/rescheduled decision boundaries and handling of commitments. Do not invent a user-approved policy. Conversation idle is always real-world 300 seconds independent of simulation clock (LEO-135).
Document safe deterministic ongoing-action behavior during model outage; decisions requiring inference remain honestly queued/paused. No fabricated dialogue, inference-LIVE implication, accumulated missed-tick calls or catch-up quota bypass.

## Work and acceptance

* Audit reuse through LEO-165, then persist stable town/object/resident IDs, world revision/epoch, tick position and schema version in Postgres. Objects, inventory, activities/progress, resident state, relationships/selected-memory references survive restart; memory selection lives in LEO-167.
* One authoritative mutation path across server processes: transaction/optimistic version and fenced writer ownership, with state and event outbox committed atomically. Redis is coordination/cache, never sole world truth.
* Typed model intent is input only. Validate allowed existing action/target IDs, range, capacity/inventory and preconditions against current committed state; apply deterministic rules or record rejection/provenance without impossible mutation. Define initial allowed-action catalog with LEO-168; public visitors cannot call it directly.
* Idempotent ticks/jobs and recovery preserve shared state without duplicate inventory/actions/events. Restore pending activity, conversation reservations/lease versions and durable inference reservation references; LEO-135/132 own reconciliation, including unknown-sent attempts.
* Viewer arrival/departure never creates/resets/stops the town or multiplies model work. World storage/progress can operate independently of model availability. Queued inference requires admission, not one call per frame.
* Publish redacted snapshots/events through LEO-136/142 with revision and monotonic sequence; private conversation/memory never enters public truth by default or accident.

## Tests / dependencies

Depends on LEO-165 gate; coordinate LEO-132 durable reservations and LEO-142 outbox contract. Implement storage before the consuming API/renderer, not after them. Test two writers racing (one commit), restart with nonempty inventory/ongoing activity, duplicate jobs, atomic outbox replay, invalid LLM action rejection and zero viewers. LEO-171 adds multi-browser/restart evidence after LEO-135/136; LEO-172 adds injection/end-to-end checks.

## Historical contract superseded

The former farm harness here specified three residents, six decisions ≥45s apart, ≤6-minute episodes, a 60s zero-viewer shutdown, memory reset, eight attempts/episode, two/day, no visitor dialogue and only a fixed farm menu. Those are historical only; the 40s authored renderer is separately LEO-90. This amendment preserves the issue/status/history; no completed autonomous engine is claimed. issues.description:
### J4 live contract

Fixture has two eligible canonical jobs and one deterministic rejection. No visitor résumé, arbitrary URL, or live scraping. Header: **“Live pipeline run on bundled sample jobs; website delivery adapter.”**
* Create a temporary SQLite database per run, preserving the actual project contract. RQ calls a pinned package/CLI adapter, not a JavaScript reimplementation. SSE exposes committed stage events. The website delivery adapter consumes the outbox and acknowledges the displayed card. It sends nothing to Leo's Discord and does not claim to test Discord transport.
* Show counts, duplicate provenance, retained conflict, eligibility reasons, fit/missing skills/concerns, threshold decisions, one card per qualifying canonical job, Apply/Skip/Open. Apply means **“mark approved in this demo; no application submitted.”** Open displays the bundled sample posting, never a purported current vacancy.
* `Repeat ingestion` within the run demonstrates stable IDs, cached scores, and no duplicate notification. An allowlisted threshold adjustment reuses scores. No new model request. Decisions are session-isolated; expire the run after one hour.
* Maximum three upstream attempts/run: two scores plus one shared retry. Total deadline 90 seconds. Malformed output stays unscored. Below-threshold results show reasons even if no match card qualifies.
* Errors remain visible in the channel: `Provider unavailable — scoring incomplete`, `Daily live sample limit reached`, or a named stage failure. Keep actual completed stages; a separate RECORDED panel provides replay. Never splice recorded success into a live transcript.
* Cache by evidence + candidate + model/provider configuration + prompt/schema version. Cached inference says `RECORDED — reused score from <time>` inside a genuinely live deterministic run. Fresh scoring requires a complete budget reservation.

### Launch budget: $0 in purchased inference

OpenRouter currently documents **50 requests/day and 20/minute** for unfunded free-model use; qualifying credit purchases increase the daily allowance. More keys do not create account quota. Availability is opportunistic, not an SLA. [OpenRouter limits](<https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits>), [published free-tier figures](<https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/how-to-get-the-lowest-cost-llm-inference-on-openrouter/>).

**Site ceiling: 40 upstream attempts per UTC day, six/minute, one in flight globally.** Deployment checks actual limits, eligibility, competing account usage; reduce this ceiling when needed. No paid fallback, auto-top-up, quota-evading key rotation, or trial-credit dependence. Free describes inference billing; NAS electricity/storage/bandwidth/maintenance still cost something.

| Reservation | Attempts/day | Max input/output tokens per attempt | Buys |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Farm | 16 | 2,000 / 256 | Two episodes, each six decisions plus two retries |
| Jobs | 12 | 3,000 / 500 | Four runs, each two scores plus one retry |
| AI-Leo | 8 | 2,500 / 400 | Eight uncached answers, no retry |
| Optional post polish | 2 | 4,000 / 1,000 | Two cleanups; long posts use deterministic formatting |
| Verification reserve | 2 | 3,000 / 500 | Smoke probes, not continual inference health checks |
| **Total** | **40** | **≤102,000 input / ≤16,296 output tokens/day** | Hard ceilings, not promised throughput |

* A server-side gateway holds the OpenRouter key. Pin tested `:free` model IDs/provider policy per feature in deployment config. No browser model/provider/key selection; no random free router for recorded comparisons. Verify zero-priced routes and schema/language behavior before release. Record exact model ID in captures; retired/unavailable model → fail closed. Model selection is a deployment gate, not a promise that today's model exists in 90 days.
* Redis atomically reserves each run's maximum attempts and enforces shared caps. Postgres durably records reservations/attempts so Redis restart cannot replenish quota. Reserve before enqueue; idempotency prevents double reservation. Failed calls/retries count conservatively. Release safely expired unused reservations; never refund unknown sent attempts. Disable implicit SDK retries and model-fallback loops.
* Budgets span locales/features and the provider account. No automatic transfer between allocations. Other account usage reduces availability; provider 429 overrides the local ledger.
* Per signed anonymous session and hashed-IP bucket: one fresh Job run/day, two AI-Leo answers/day, one farm-create request/day. Watching/replay consumes no model quota. Use short-lived capabilities, origin checks, payload limits and gateway limits together; CORS is not abuse prevention. Distributed abuse can still exhaust the allowance; accept replay as the degraded experience.
* Honor Retry-After; do not hold visitors through long throttles. Circuit-break repeated errors/exhaustion. Message: “Today's live allowance is used; explore the recorded example.” Do not promise an unverified provider reset time.

Authenticated streams use fetch streaming with capability headers, not tokens in SSE query URLs. Events carry run ID, monotonic sequence, server timestamp, provenance, execution kind. Commit state/outbox atomically; publisher fans out to Redis Streams. FastAPI streams without occupying an RQ worker per viewer. Reconnect from last sequence; trimmed history returns a snapshot plus sequence. Drop slow clients, never unbounded buffers. Cap public streams at 50, two/session; queued inference jobs at eight, admission wait at 15 seconds. Excess clients receive static fallback immediately.

| Transition | Visitor behavior |
| -- | -- |
| Initial load | Finished static scene/evidence, no blank loading shell |
| Live requested | “Queued” beside baseline; 202 alone never makes evidence LIVE |
| Fresh committed event/result | LIVE for execution, timestamp/model; input still says bundled where appropriate |
| No heartbeat for 20s, stale event, or run failure | UNKNOWN current status; last timestamp/completed stages retained; separate RECORDED option |
| Episode completes | Stop LIVE badge; captured trace becomes RECORDED with completion time |
| Cache/replay selected | RECORDED even if animated or delivered by online API |
| Capture missing/corrupt | UNKNOWN evidence; authored conclusion/diagram retained; illustration never relabeled capture |
| Redis/NAS/provider down | Admission closes; no unaccounted calls; static site remains usable |

### Acceptance criteria

* **Accounting:** concurrent creation/retries/worker interruption/Redis restart/model retirement/429/malformed JSON cannot bypass budgets, make paid calls, or cross sessions. Probes count.
* **Jobs:** seven observations preserve provenance; requisition conflicts retained; filter reasons visible; only eligible jobs score; no duplicate card on repeat; Apply only changes demo; incomplete scores remain incomplete.

issues.title: M2 · Concurrency, accounting, isolation and recovery acceptance
issues.description:
| Milestone | Build in order | Ship gate / exclusions |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **Day 60 — farm and Jobs live** | Service entries; gateway accounting, queue isolation, outbox/SSE/reconnect/kill switches. T3 shared episodes; passive H4. J4 real sample pipeline/outbox/review/cache rerun. Complete OpenCode recorded animations for verified features; unresolved ones marked. | Rejection/timeout, shared viewers, isolated job actions, idempotency, restart, quota/provider/NAS failure checks pass. Daily cap 40. No public coding instance. |

### Launch budget: $0 in purchased inference

OpenRouter currently documents **50 requests/day and 20/minute** for unfunded free-model use; qualifying credit purchases increase the daily allowance. More keys do not create account quota. Availability is opportunistic, not an SLA. [OpenRouter limits](<https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits>), [published free-tier figures](<https://openrouter.ai/blog/tutorials/how-to-get-the-lowest-cost-llm-inference-on-openrouter/>).

**Site ceiling: 40 upstream attempts per UTC day, six/minute, one in flight globally.** Deployment checks actual limits, eligibility, competing account usage; reduce this ceiling when needed. No paid fallback, auto-top-up, quota-evading key rotation, or trial-credit dependence. Free describes inference billing; NAS electricity/storage/bandwidth/maintenance still cost something.

| Reservation | Attempts/day | Max input/output tokens per attempt | Buys |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| Farm | 16 | 2,000 / 256 | Two episodes, each six decisions plus two retries |
| Jobs | 12 | 3,000 / 500 | Four runs, each two scores plus one retry |
| AI-Leo | 8 | 2,500 / 400 | Eight uncached answers, no retry |
| Optional post polish | 2 | 4,000 / 1,000 | Two cleanups; long posts use deterministic formatting |
| Verification reserve | 2 | 3,000 / 500 | Smoke probes, not continual inference health checks |
| **Total** | **40** | **≤102,000 input / ≤16,296 output tokens/day** | Hard ceilings, not promised throughput |

* A server-side gateway holds the OpenRouter key. Pin tested `:free` model IDs/provider policy per feature in deployment config. No browser model/provider/key selection; no random free router for recorded comparisons. Verify zero-priced routes and schema/language behavior before release. Record exact model ID in captures; retired/unavailable model → fail closed. Model selection is a deployment gate, not a promise that today's model exists in 90 days.
* Redis atomically reserves each run's maximum attempts and enforces shared caps. Postgres durably records reservations/attempts so Redis restart cannot replenish quota. Reserve before enqueue; idempotency prevents double reservation. Failed calls/retries count conservatively. Release safely expired unused reservations; never refund unknown sent attempts. Disable implicit SDK retries and model-fallback loops.
* Budgets span locales/features and the provider account. No automatic transfer between allocations. Other account usage reduces availability; provider 429 overrides the local ledger.
* Per signed anonymous session and hashed-IP bucket: one fresh Job run/day, two AI-Leo answers/day, one farm-create request/day. Watching/replay consumes no model quota. Use short-lived capabilities, origin checks, payload limits and gateway limits together; CORS is not abuse prevention. Distributed abuse can still exhaust the allowance; accept replay as the degraded experience.
* Honor Retry-After; do not hold visitors through long throttles. Circuit-break repeated errors/exhaustion. Message: “Today's live allowance is used; explore the recorded example.” Do not promise an unverified provider reset time.

| Transition | Visitor behavior |
| -- | -- |
| Initial load | Finished static scene/evidence, no blank loading shell |
| Live requested | “Queued” beside baseline; 202 alone never makes evidence LIVE |
| Fresh committed event/result | LIVE for execution, timestamp/model; input still says bundled where appropriate |
| No heartbeat for 20s, stale event, or run failure | UNKNOWN current status; last timestamp/completed stages retained; separate RECORDED option |
| Episode completes | Stop LIVE badge; captured trace becomes RECORDED with completion time |
| Cache/replay selected | RECORDED even if animated or delivered by online API |
| Capture missing/corrupt | UNKNOWN evidence; authored conclusion/diagram retained; illustration never relabeled capture |
| Redis/NAS/provider down | Admission closes; no unaccounted calls; static site remains usable |

Authenticated streams use fetch streaming with capability headers, not tokens in SSE query URLs. Events carry run ID, monotonic sequence, server timestamp, provenance, execution kind. Commit state/outbox atomically; publisher fans out to Redis Streams. FastAPI streams without occupying an RQ worker per viewer. Reconnect from last sequence; trimmed history returns a snapshot plus sequence. Drop slow clients, never unbounded buffers. Cap public streams at 50, two/session; queued inference jobs at eight, admission wait at 15 seconds. Excess clients receive static fallback immediately.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Resilience:** disable JS/disconnect NAS; check both roots, core deep links, one article per available locale, posters, preview base path. No false LIVE on replay/cache.
* **Accounting:** concurrent creation/retries/worker interruption/Redis restart/model retirement/429/malformed JSON cannot bypass budgets, make paid calls, or cross sessions. Probes count.
* **Jobs:** seven observations preserve provenance; requisition conflicts retained; filter reasons visible; only eligible jobs score; no duplicate card on repeat; Apply only changes demo; incomplete scores remain incomplete.
* **Farm:** observation isolation, invalid-action rejection, one writer, replay from committed events, SSE resume, zero-viewer shutdown. Captured actions replay deterministically; rerunning LLM does not promise identical decisions.
* Exercise simultaneous shared farm viewers, separate Jobs sessions, timeout/rejection, idempotency, Redis restart, provider/NAS outages and honest replay labels.
