issues.title: L · AI-Leo approved corpus and retrieval architecture
issues.description:
### AI-Leo retrieval architecture

* Start with approved bio, résumé, public project summaries, short opinion answers. Leo's home audio/video adds evidence when recorded; it is not a launch dependency. Never ingest general kimaki history, DMs, calendars, NAS folders, or Jellyfin libraries.
* Private ingestion stores selected originals on the NAS. RQ CPU transcription processes recordings; Leo corrects/approves transcript and publishable excerpts. Only approved excerpts enter the public corpus. Raw home recordings remain private; media citations require separately approved clips.
* Postgres stores source ID, approval, date, language, revision, public anchor, optional timecode, supersession links. Chunk \~300 tokens with 50-token overlap. Version a small lexical index; Chinese uses explicit segmentation/character n-grams. Maintain approved bilingual aliases for skills/project names.
* Reuse AI Society's evidence/validity concepts and compatible contracts through a pinned adapter. Its production embedding adapter is unfinished: do not instantiate it or change research thresholds to ship the website. **First release is lexical retrieval plus generation; RAG does not require a vector database.** Defer semantic embeddings until they improve a held-out question set.
* `POST /api/demos/leo/answers`: ≤500 characters, at most two previous turns, signed 15-minute session. Retrieve up to four approved passages, ≤1,200 tokens; total prompt ≤2,500 tokens. No matching evidence → immediate abstention, zero model calls. “Current” facts use latest approved nonsuperseded source and show its date; conflicts/staleness do not become current fact.
* RQ makes one free request, ≤400 output tokens, no model retry, 35-second total deadline. Schema: answer, cited source IDs, unsupported flag. Reject unknown citations. Distinguish Leo's stated opinion from synthesis; never invent a stronger skill ranking. Citation validation cannot guarantee entailment; evaluate separately.
* Return validated answer plus excerpts. Cache only three public starter questions by locale/corpus revision/prompt/model; outputs say RECORDED. Arbitrary questions stay ephemeral, expire after 15 minutes, never update Leo's memory or enter permanent conversation logs.
* Before submission: “Your question and public source excerpts are sent to an external model provider. Don't include private information.” Keep routing privacy restrictions fixed; incompatible provider → source-only fallback, not relaxed settings. Outage shows authored FAQ and `UNKNOWN — no answer generated`.

### Acceptance criteria

* **AI-Leo:** freeze 24 questions: eight factual, four opinions, four current/correction, four unsupported/private, four injection attempts, distributed across English/Chinese. Require approved valid citations for factual claims, no invented biography/opinion, correct supersession, abstention on every unsupported case. Leo reviews voice/meaning. Any violation blocks free-form Q&A; authored FAQ ships. This is a release check, not a claimed accuracy benchmark.
* **Publisher/privacy:** wrong author/stale Publish rejected; duplicate events yield one draft; malformed media/Markdown cannot execute scripts; deployment recoverable; no originals/drafts/secrets/Jellyfin/private text in public output/history. Published content hash verified.
* Verify bilingual lexical retrieval, approval/supersession, dated anchors and no-source zero-call abstention; recordings remain optional and originals private.

issues.title: §13 · Risk decisions and release exclusions
issues.description:
## 13. RISK FLAGS — decisions, not an everything-list

| Risk / conflict | Recommendation | Release boundary |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Multiple live ideas contradict one-demo law | Explicit one simulation + two bounded tools; no public OpenCode; passive Home | No fourth inference surface during 90 days |
| Free models cannot sustain always-on farm | Two short shared episodes/day; recorded default | No continuous-inference claim or silent paid fallback |
| Farm shortcut misrepresents AI Society | Adaptation label, reused/replaced modules, no steering/fidelity claim | Label adjacent to exhibit |
| AI-Leo invents personal facts/opinions | Approved corpus, dates, corrections, abstention, no memory writes | Grounded-answer checks before live submission |
| End-to-end Jobs implies live discovery/Discord | Real pipeline on bundled input with website outbox; explicit boundaries | No current-vacancy/Discord-verification/auto-apply claim |
| Animation hides conclusions or weak evidence | Finished diagram first; four explanatory sequences with trace or illustration label | No fake metrics/unsupported authorship/autoplay maze |
| Gallery duplicates Home or becomes hub | One finite page, direct Home links, PC inline | No filters/nested gallery/new PC page |
| 3D PC consumes time/mobile budget | Poster/clip after core, two-day cap; defer WebGL | No Home dependency; omit unfinished card |
| Live2D intrusive or implies a real digital person | Still first; optional L3 event gestures | ≤2 MB optional rig, rights verified, no loop; otherwise still |
| Secret pages leak NAS | Tailscale private origin plus service authentication; reuse Jellyfin | No private data in Pages/repo/feeds/source maps |
| Public OpenCode abused despite fixed models | Public recorded showcase, private capture instance | Excluded from day 90, not hidden behind obscure URL |
| Discord bot publishes private chatter | Dedicated selection, owner allowlist, preview, hash-bound Publish | No publish-every-message or model-controlled deploy |
| Chinese doubles maintenance | Shared assets/structure, revision-linked core mirrors, asynchronous articles | No unlabeled English fallback |
| Domain/infra docs disagree | Apex AGENTS rule; inspect and prepare corrected release runbook | Old-repo cutover needs Leo approval after artifact review |
| Distributed visitors drain free quota | Finite allocations/admission; accept degradation | Exhaustion remains usable recorded site |

## 0. Laws and explicit revisions

1. **No puzzle required.** Show the conclusion, finished state, and concrete example before interaction. Motion explains an already visible result.
2. **One shared live simulation: Tiny World.** Explicitly revise “one live demo total” to admit two bounded, opt-in tools: a Job Matching run and an AI-Leo answer. These are additional live features; calling them previews does not erase their cost. No model calls on page load. No public OpenCode terminal. The farm runs short episodes, not 24/7 inference.
3. **Everything past Home is opt-in depth.** Add one Projects gallery. Home still links directly to the strongest case studies; the gallery is never a mandatory intermediate stop.
4. **Proof is inline.** No evidence drawers, nested demo hub, canvas dedup graph, standalone build-log, or standalone infrastructure visualization. Technical disclosures contain supporting detail, not conclusions.
5. **Uncertainty stays visible.** Keep the ambiguous merge, rejected world action, unsupported personal answer, and failed coding-tool run.
6. **Truthful states:** `LIVE`, `RECORDED`, `UNKNOWN`. A live connection does not prove live inference. Label input provenance and output execution separately. Never say “waking server…” without a real wake mechanism.
7. **Static first.** Public routes, articles, conclusions, images, and replays come from GitHub Pages. FastAPI on the NAS owns live work. NAS failure must not prevent reading the site.
8. **Honest authorship.** Distinguish Leo's projects, upstream modifications, companion tools, third-party components, licensed/generated art, illustrations, and verified captures. AI-Leo is not Leo speaking live.
9. **Personality has a budget.** Keep anime and recipes. Give the farm warmth. Reserve PC assembly for one small gallery exhibit. No game-lobby Home or floating avatar everywhere.

### Acceptance criteria

* **Story:** a reader identifies Leo, three projects, email/résumé from Home without clicking. Every case has visible result, limit, authorship.

Require approved valid citations for factual claims, no invented biography/opinion, correct supersession, abstention on every unsupported case. Leo reviews voice/meaning. Any violation blocks free-form Q&A; authored FAQ ships. This is a release check, not a claimed accuracy benchmark.
* **Publisher/privacy:** wrong author/stale Publish rejected; duplicate events yield one draft; malformed media/Markdown cannot execute scripts; deployment recoverable; no originals/drafts/secrets/Jellyfin/private text in public output/history. Published content hash verified.

### Scope

* Build a FontTools instancer + pyftsubset pipeline for self-hosted Latin WOFF2 subsets: Newsreader display with pinned opsz and wght 400–600; Source Sans 3 UI/body with wght 400–650.

* Measure ≤100 KB of fonts per route; do not assume subset estimates satisfy the budget. Measure image-heavy and farm pages before locking typography.

* Builds emit subset fonts and matching CSS for both locales.
* Record measured font bytes per route and verify each stays ≤100 KB.
* Pages render correctly with downloaded fonts disabled.

issues.description:
Storyboard: `tasks/site-v2-storyboard.md`, §14 day-30 acceptance + §1 global elements.
Decision: D4 in [LEO-160 · ADR · v2 tooling decisions](<https://linear.app/leochai/issue/LEO-160/adr-v2-tooling-decisions-ratified-2026-09-11>) (ratified 2026-09-11).
Build order: M1 · Static story (day 30); child of LEO-58.

### Scope

* Configure Playwright Test projects: Chromium no-JS; Chromium JS + `@axe-core/playwright`; mobile + reduced-motion; Firefox/WebKit smoke.
* Run lychee offline link/fragment checking with `--include-fragments`, `--index-files`, and `--root-dir`, staging preview output under the real `/leochai-website/` prefix.
* Run html-validate on generated HTML. Run local Lighthouse CI as a diagnostic, not a release gate.
* Build a Python site-contract validator for expected canonical routes, translation groups, a legacy-URL fixture, canonical/hreflang reciprocity, sitemap-vs-routes, robots placement, and RSS via a pinned W3C feed validator plus policy assertions.
* Enforce the 500 KB cold-visit budget using encoded response bodies for all actually loaded resources, including every font, image and trace, at desktop + mobile, initial load AND post-scroll, for both production `/` and preview `/leochai-website/` targets.
* Provide one orchestration script: build once per target → validate that exact candidate artifact → promote the same bytes with a hash manifest. Include exit traps and keep reports outside the artifact.

### Key constraints

* Run locally/on NAS; no GitHub Actions.
* Never rebuild between validation and promotion; build, validate and promote each prefix target separately.
* Failed validation never touches the published checkout.
* Preserve `CNAME` and `.nojekyll`; use `scripts/publish.sh` with normal commit + push, no force-push.
* Reading remains independent of NAS: “server-rendered” means build-generated static HTML.

### Acceptance criteria

* Deliberate breakages are each caught: a broken link, a missing required zh route, a page exceeding the budget, and bad hreflang.
* A clean build validates and promotes; the hash manifest proves the promoted bytes match the validated candidate.
* Validation failure leaves the published checkout unchanged.
* A 404 probe passes with a real not-found response, with no SPA fallback masking a missing route.
* Both prefix targets pass the configured browser, link/fragment, HTML, site-contract and resource-budget checks.

Specification: requirements are reproduced here so this issue can be implemented from Linear.

* The route inventory, translation groups, alias and RSS policy assertions IMPLEMENT the contracts in LEO-112, LEO-113, LEO-128, LEO-129 — read those before extending fixtures; this issue owns the harness, they own the contracts.

## Agreed direction and scope

One shared persistent town runs continuously on Leo's existing NAS, with five AI facets and visitor text conversation. This is a feasibility/decision slice (planning target 0.5–2 engineer-days, not a delivery promise); do not provision while auditing.

## Work and acceptance

* Inspect actual NAS CPU model/cores, installed and available RAM, GPU/VRAM (including whether none exists), current services/load and practical headroom. Record evidence and unknowns, not inferred hardware.
* Audit existing AI Society modules by repository revision/path: observations, memory/retrieval, context, scheduler/planning, action validation, persistence and model adapter. List reuse unchanged / bounded adapter / missing, with actual contracts and small verification evidence. Do not assume unfinished embedding or cognitive modules work; no private files or kimaki history ingestion.
* Preserve static GitHub Pages plus existing NAS FastAPI/Postgres/Redis/RQ, Caddy/DDNS. Identify reusable service/queue/storage boundaries before proposing additions; no hosting migration. Later implementation records hosting in services/README.md and actual infra changes in docs/infra.md.
* Estimate five residents' routine/event decision load plus bounded visitor chat, context/output needs, latency and outage tolerance. Continuous life uses deterministic ticks and decisions at boundaries/events, not inference every frame.
* Choose a suitable local model only against measured capacity and documented language/schema/latency suitability, or present an external-model option for explicit Leo approval of model, cost ceiling, latency and privacy. Distinguish measured results from estimates; no paid benchmark calls/new capacity. State unresolved checks if a model cannot yet be evaluated without provisioning.
* Record a gate verdict, chosen route (or unresolved alternatives), operational caps to feed LEO-132 and the town admission ticket, and required approval evidence. This gate must close before backend/inference provisioning. No paid calls/new capacity until the decision; no external paid route without explicit approval.

## Budget contradiction resolved

The old 40-attempt/day site plan, farm 16/day, two episodes/day and eight attempts/episode describe the superseded short-episode town and cannot deliver continuous LLM life. They are not an implicit town budget. Do not raise spend or consume Jobs 12/day, AI-Leo 8/day, polish 2/day or verification 2/day; unrelated existing ceilings stay effective. Record any proposed account-wide change for Leo's decision, never silently apply it.

## Dependencies / output

Starts with read-only inspection; no art/Home approval needed to document feasibility. Downstream: LEO-144 world, persona/context, planner and bounded admission; shared owners LEO-59/130 (NAS), LEO-60/132 (accounting). Open: actual capability, module fitness, local model choice or approved external budget/latency/privacy.

## Supplied read-only reuse audit — source evidence, not deployment validation

Leo supplied this completed audit on 2026-09-12:

* ai-society at c0df3b9: world/sim.py provides real action authority/preconditions; shared world state and memory/store.py are in-memory.
* state/store.py provides transactional per-person SQLite patterns that may be reused; it is not durable town persistence.
* runtime/pipeline.py uses FakeModel echo, not autonomous inference.
* scripts/person_poc/qwen.py performs real local Qwen generation, but a deterministic decision is chosen BEFORE model speech. It does not establish an autonomous town agent.
* personal-api at 05b4005 supplies FastAPI/Postgres/RQ scaffolding; no town routes exist.

Use these revisions/paths as the audit baseline and inspect integration contracts as needed; do not redo the completed inventory without cause. Source inspection does not prove deployment, hardware capacity, working autonomous life or end-to-end integration. Actual NAS capability and model-capacity/latency/privacy decision remain unresolved gates.

Sizing: 0.5–2 engineer-days describes intended bounded subtask size, never a full-delivery estimate. Leo's current full-integration assessment is approximately 15–25% complete effort-wise; this is a planning estimate, not measured functional coverage, a completion/status change or an approved launch claim.

Remote routing removes the local-GPU prerequisite, but durable world/clock/restart, production privacy/provider disclosure, shared budget/accounting, capacity/availability and action-validation integration remain open. Planning/Linear scope only in this pass: no file changes, implementation, worker dispatch, merge, model/container calls or callbacks. Future sole builder Luna xhigh, then independent Claude Opus5 review. Preserve other project allocations and NAS restrictions; isolated stdlib checks only.

## Scope

Scenario-based integration tests for the persistent town, using controlled clocks/model responses and multiple API/worker processes plus two browsers. ## Required scenarios / acceptance

4. Expiry/goodbye safely resumes or reassesses paused activity. Disconnection alone does not silently release; reconnect follows the explicitly decided semantics and cannot extend beyond idle without an accepted message.
5. Late model replies, delayed queued work and replayed capabilities after release/reclaim/version change cannot mutate world, plan, dialogue or memories. Include expiry while inference is in flight.
6. Restart API/world worker/Redis with claimed conversations and in-flight inference. Restore objects, inventory, activity, character/context references, relationships, memories, clock and reservations. Reconcile real-time expired leases; fence old workers and preserve unknown-sent budget reservations without replenishment.
7. Outbox retry, event duplication/history trimming and server epoch change recover clients from the authoritative snapshot. No public reset or viewer-count shutdown.
8. Zero viewers and model unavailability follow the documented LEO-144 clock/outage policy; recovery does not issue catch-up call storms or exceed approved admission.

issues.title: Conversation reservation core: atomic ownership, idle expiry and fencing (Luna trial)
issues.description:
## Purpose and authorization boundary

One bounded backend calibration trial under LEO-135: an isolated Python/SQLAlchemy PostgreSQL persistence/domain library exercised by synthetic callers only. This child is runnable locally because it makes no deployed or full-endpoint claim. Creating this issue is a documentation action only; do not start implementation, provision infrastructure or deploy as part of issue creation.

LEO-135 remains Backlog with its existing blockers LEO-144, LEO-165, LEO-131, LEO-169 and LEO-60 unchanged. This child does not resolve privacy, model capacity, town clock/restart policy, inference admission or world integration. Completing it cannot mark the parent Done.

## Contract

* At most one owner per resident across processes, enforced atomically in PostgreSQL. Use resident-scoped unforgeable capability verification and persist synthetic owner/resident IDs, capability verifier, reservation state, last accepted message timestamp and a durable monotonically increasing version/fencing counter. No raw chat text or real visitor data in storage, events, logs or tests.
* Reservation begins with the first accepted visitor message in the synthetic test adapter. This is a test-only adapter convention; product initial-claim semantics remain OPEN in LEO-135.
* A newly accepted owner visitor message records authoritative server real time. The reservation is invalid at exactly 300 real-world seconds after last_accepted_visitor_message_at, independent of simulation ticks. Only a new accepted owner message renews.
* Duplicate retries, rejected/wrong-owner messages, model results, heartbeats, watching and capability reattachment do not renew. Specify idempotency keys for claim/message/goodbye, including retry after release/reclaim; return consistent busy/expired/invalid outcomes. A duplicate claim cannot recreate or extend an old reservation.
